newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian radio spectrum auctions set in Feb.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian radio spectrum auctions set in Feb.

text.p: The Australian government's Spectrum Management Authority (SMA) would begin auctions for rights to radio spectrum in the 500-megahertz band on February 3, a spokesman said on Friday.
SMA marketing manager Ian Hayne said the 500 MHz auctions -- the first of their type in the world -- had generated interest from 13 bidders and initial revenue of about A$500,000 through deposits.
"We're very pleased with the interest -- it's been good," Hayne told Reuters, adding that the majority of the interest had come from local companies and individuals.
"There's only one multinational involved," he said.

The 500 MHz band is generally used for two-way radios and radio-based telephone systems such as that run by government-owned telecoms carrier Telstra Corp in remote areas. The auction of 15-year licences to 17 areas in that bandwidth are seen as a test run in the lead up to the September quarter sale of rights to the 1800 MHz band.

The 1800 MHz auctions are expected to generate vast interest both internationally and locally because of the bandwidth's suitability for mobile telephony, including the widely-used European DCS-1800 system.
An industry report last year estimated the 1800 MHz auctions could reap between A$900 million and A$2.4 billion for the Australian government.
Asked how much the SMA expected to raise from the 500 MHz auctions, Hayne said: "We really have no idea at this stage."

The auctions will be the first in the world where buyers will have the right to use their spectrum bandwidth for any type of technology, as opposed to auctions in the U.S. where bidders buy the right to use it for a specific technology only.
